questions.question: What command sets a file permission to rwxr-xr-- for owner, group, others?
questions.explanation: Octal permissions: owner(rwx=7), group(r-x=5), others(r--=4) = 754. chmod 754 file sets this. Alternatively: chmod u=rwx,g=rx,o=r file. Use ls -l to verify.

questions.question: How do you make a systemd service start automatically at boot?
questions.explanation: systemctl enable service: creates symlinks in /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/ so service starts at boot. systemctl enable --now service: enable AND start immediately. systemctl disable: remove autostart. systemctl is-enabled: check status.

questions.question: What command creates a logical volume of 5G named 'data' in VG 'vg0'?
questions.explanation: lvcreate -L 5G -n data vg0: -L size, -n name, vg0 is the volume group. After: mkfs.xfs /dev/vg0/data → mount. -l for LE units: -l 100%FREE uses all free space. lvs: list logical volumes.

questions.question: How do you persistently mount /dev/vg0/data to /mnt/data with xfs filesystem?
questions.explanation: /etc/fstab format: device mountpoint filesystem options dump pass. defaults = rw,suid,dev,exec,auto,nouser,async. 0 0 = no dump, no fsck. After editing: mount -a to test without reboot. Use blkid to get UUID for more reliable mounting.

questions.question: What is SELinux and what are its three modes?
options: A mandatory access control system — Enforcing (policies enforced, violations blocked+logged), Permissive (not enforced but logged), Disabled (completely off). getenforce to check, setenforce 0/1 for temporary change
questions.explanation: SELinux: mandatory access control beyond DAC (discretionary). Enforcing: production mode. Permissive: troubleshooting (logs denials, doesn't block). Disabled: requires reboot. /etc/selinux/config for persistent change. semanage, restorecon, ausearch -m avc: key tools.

questions.question: How do you find all files owned by user 'alice' under /var?
questions.explanation: find /var -user alice: finds all files owned by alice. find /var -group devs: by group. find /var -perm /4000: find SUID files. find /var -mtime -7: modified in last 7 days. find /var -size +100M: files > 100MB. -exec rm {} \; to act on results.

questions.question: What command shows currently open firewall ports using firewalld?
questions.explanation: firewall-cmd --list-all: shows active zone, interfaces, sources, services, ports. --list-ports: ports only. --list-services: services only. Add port: firewall-cmd --add-port=8080/tcp --permanent then --reload. firewall-cmd --zone=public --add-service=http --permanent.

questions.question: How do you extend an existing XFS filesystem after expanding the LV?
questions.explanation: Expand LV: lvextend -L +10G /dev/vg0/data. Extend XFS: xfs_growfs /mnt/data (use mount point, not device). XFS can be grown while mounted. ext4: resize2fs /dev/vg0/data (use device). Always expand LV first, then filesystem.

questions.question: What is the purpose of cron and how do you edit the crontab?
options: Schedule recurring tasks — crontab -e to edit, format: minute hour day month weekday command
questions.explanation: crontab format: */5 * * * * /path/to/script (every 5 min). Fields: min(0-59) hour(0-23) day(1-31) month(1-12) weekday(0-7). crontab -l: list. crontab -r: remove. /etc/crontab: system cron with user field. /etc/cron.d/: additional cron files. systemd timers: modern alternative.

questions.question: How do you create a user 'bob' with UID 1500, home directory /home/bob, and shell /bin/bash?
questions.explanation: useradd -u 1500 -m -s /bin/bash bob: -u UID, -m create home, -s shell. Set password: passwd bob. -g primary group: -g groupname. -G supplementary groups: -G wheel,docker. View: id bob. Modify existing user: usermod. Delete: userdel -r bob (remove home).

questions.question: What does the sticky bit do on a directory?
options: Prevents users from deleting files they don't own in a shared directory — only file owner or root can delete. Set with chmod +t /shared or chmod 1777 /shared. Example: /tmp has sticky bit
questions.explanation: Sticky bit (chmod +t or mode 1xxx): files in directory can only be deleted by: file owner, directory owner, or root. Common on /tmp (world-writable but users can't delete each other's files). ls -ld shows 't' in others execute position. chmod 1777 /shared sets sticky+rwxrwxrwx.

questions.question: How do you configure a static IP on RHEL/CentOS using nmcli?
options: nmcli con mod eth0 ipv4.addresses 192.168.1.10/24 ipv4.gateway 192.168.1.1 ipv4.method manual; nmcli con up eth0
questions.explanation: nmcli con mod CONNECTION ipv4.addresses IP/MASK ipv4.gateway GW ipv4.dns DNS ipv4.method manual. Then nmcli con up CONNECTION. Persistent. nmcli con show: list connections. nmcli device status: device states. Alternatively: edit /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/CONNECTION.nmconnection.

questions.question: What command displays all systemd service logs in real-time?
questions.explanation: journalctl -f: follow (like tail -f). journalctl -u nginx: logs for specific unit. journalctl -xe: recent logs with explanations. journalctl --since '1 hour ago': time filter. journalctl -p err: error level and above. journalctl --disk-usage: storage used. /var/log/messages: traditional syslog, may still exist.

questions.question: How do you schedule a one-time task to run at 3pm today?
questions.explanation: at command: at 15:00 (enter commands, Ctrl+D to finish). at now + 1 hour. atq: list scheduled at jobs. atrm JOB_NUM: remove. Service: atd must be running. For recurring: use cron. at is for one-time delayed execution.

questions.question: What is the purpose of /etc/sudoers and how do you safely edit it?
options: Configure user permissions — edit directly with vi
Configure sudo access — always edit with visudo which validates syntax before saving. Syntax: user ALL=(ALL) ALL or %group ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/specific_command
questions.explanation: visudo: opens /etc/sudoers in editor with syntax checking — prevents saving invalid syntax that would break sudo for all users. %wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL: all wheel group members can sudo. User bob can restart nginx without password: bob ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl restart nginx. /etc/sudoers.d/: drop-in files.

questions.question: How do you list all available SELinux booleans related to httpd?
questions.explanation: getsebool -a: list all booleans with current values. getsebool httpd_can_network_connect: specific boolean. setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect on: set persistently (-P). Common booleans: httpd_can_network_connect (allow Apache to make outbound connections), httpd_use_nfs (allow serving NFS-mounted content).

questions.question: What command adds a user to the supplementary group 'wheel'?
questions.explanation: usermod -aG wheel username: -a (append, don't replace other groups), -G (supplementary group). Without -a: replaces ALL supplementary groups! gpasswd -a username wheel: alternative. id username: verify. User needs to re-login for group change to take effect (or: newgrp wheel in current session).

questions.question: How do you create a swap partition and enable it persistently?
questions.explanation: Steps: (1) fdisk/parted to create partition with type 82 (Linux swap). (2) mkswap /dev/sdb2. (3) swapon /dev/sdb2 (immediate). (4) /etc/fstab: '/dev/sdb2 swap swap defaults 0 0'. swapon -s: show active swap. free -h: memory + swap stats. swapfile: dd + mkswap + swapon works too.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the /etc/hosts file and how does it interact with DNS?
options: Maps hostnames to IP addresses locally — consulted before DNS by default (controlled by /etc/nsswitch.conf: hosts: files dns). Entries: IP hostname aliases. Use for: local development, override DNS, emergency DNS bypass
questions.explanation: /etc/hosts: IP FQDN aliases per line. /etc/nsswitch.conf hosts: files dns — 'files' means check /etc/hosts first. For testing: add temporary entry. /etc/resolv.conf: DNS server configuration (nameserver IP, domain, search). hostnamectl: set system hostname. dnsdomainname: show domain.

questions.question: How do you set the default target (runlevel equivalent) to multi-user (non-graphical)?
questions.explanation: systemctl set-default multi-user.target: non-graphical multi-user (like runlevel 3). graphical.target: desktop (runlevel 5). rescue.target: single-user maintenance. systemctl isolate multi-user.target: switch immediately (kills graphical). systemctl get-default: check current default target.

questions.question: What command archives and compresses a directory into a .tar.gz file?
questions.explanation: tar -czvf: -c create, -z gzip compression, -v verbose, -f filename. Extract: tar -xzvf archive.tar.gz. List contents: tar -tzvf. To specific dir: tar -xzvf archive.tar.gz -C /target/. .tar.bz2: use -j instead of -z. .tar.xz: use -J. --exclude=PATTERN to exclude files.

questions.question: What is a RHEL subscription and how do you register a system?
options: Red Hat subscription provides access to repos and support — subscription-manager register --username=USER --password=PASS registers the system with Red Hat. subscription-manager attach --auto: attach available subscriptions. subscription-manager list: see attached subs
questions.explanation: RHEL subscription: required for yum/dnf updates and support. subscription-manager register: authenticate with RHSM (Red Hat Subscription Management) or Satellite. subscription-manager status: check. subscription-manager repos --list: see available repos. In RHEL 8+: insights-client --register for Red Hat Insights.

questions.question: How do you restore SELinux file contexts to their default?
questions.explanation: restorecon -Rv /path: -R recursive, -v verbose. Restores contexts based on policy defaults (/etc/selinux/targeted/contexts/files/). Use after: moving files (context doesn't follow move), creating new files in wrong location. matchpathcon -V: verify contexts. semanage fcontext: add custom file context rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between hard links and soft links (symlinks)?
options: Hard link: another directory entry pointing to same inode — same inode number, same data. Survives original deletion. Same filesystem only. Soft link: points to path/name, not inode — breaks if original deleted. Can cross filesystems. ln vs ln -s
questions.explanation: Hard link: ln source dest. Same inode. Deleting original doesn't break link. Cannot link directories (normally). Same filesystem only. Soft link: ln -s /path/to/source dest. Different inode (stores path). Breaks if source deleted/moved. Can cross filesystems, link directories, point to non-existent paths.

questions.question: How do you configure time synchronization with chrony?
options: chronyc add server ntp.example.com; systemctl restart chronyd
questions.explanation: chrony (RHEL 7+): /etc/chrony.conf — server ntp.example.com iburst. systemctl restart chronyd. chronyc sources: show NTP sources. chronyc tracking: show sync status. timedatectl: set timezone and check sync status. timedatectl list-timezones. timedatectl set-timezone America/New_York. chronyd preferred over ntpd in RHEL 7+.

questions.question: What is ACL (Access Control List) and how do you set one?
options: Extended permissions beyond owner/group/other — allows granting specific permissions to specific users/groups. setfacl -m u:alice:rw file: give alice read+write. getfacl file: view ACLs. Filesystem must be mounted with acl option
questions.explanation: ACL: setfacl -m u:USER:PERMS file, setfacl -m g:GROUP:PERMS file, setfacl -m o::PERMS file. -x: remove entry. -b: remove all ACLs. -R: recursive. Default ACL for directory (-d): inherited by new files. getfacl file: shows all ACL entries. Filesystem needs acl mount option (default on ext4/xfs in RHEL).

questions.question: How do you add a network route temporarily and permanently?
options: Temporary: ip route add NETWORK/MASK via GW; Permanent: add to nmcli connection: nmcli con mod CON ipv4.routes 'NETWORK/MASK GW'
questions.explanation: Temporary: ip route add 192.168.10.0/24 via 10.0.0.1 (lost on reboot). Permanent (NetworkManager): nmcli con mod CONNECTION ipv4.routes '192.168.10.0/24 10.0.0.1' then nmcli con up CONNECTION. Or edit connection file. ip route show: display routing table.

questions.question: What does the umask value control?
options: The default permission mask applied when new files and directories are created — subtracts from maximum permissions. umask 022: files created as 644 (666-022), dirs as 755 (777-022). Lower umask = more permissive defaults
questions.explanation: umask: subtracted from max (files=666, dirs=777). umask 022: files=644, dirs=755 (common default). umask 027: files=640, dirs=750 (more secure). Set in: /etc/profile (system), ~/.bashrc (user). umask without args: shows current. Doesn't affect existing files.

questions.question: How do you search for a package and install it with dnf?
options: dnf search httpd; dnf install httpd
yum search httpd; yum install httpd
apt search httpd; apt install httpd
questions.explanation: dnf search httpd: find packages. dnf info httpd: details. dnf install httpd: install. dnf remove httpd: uninstall. dnf update: update all. dnf upgrade: update + obsoletes. dnf list installed: installed packages. dnf provides /usr/sbin/httpd: which package provides file. dnf history: transaction history.

questions.question: What command checks disk usage of directories?
questions.explanation: du -sh /path: -s summary (total), -h human readable. du -h --max-depth=1 /var: one level deep. du -sh *: all items in current dir. df -h: filesystem disk space (mounted filesystems). df -i: inode usage. lsblk: block devices. fdisk -l: partition table.

questions.question: How do you configure password aging policies for a user?
questions.explanation: chage -M 90: max days before password must change. -m 1: minimum days between changes. -W 7: warn 7 days before expiry. -l username: list current aging info. -E 2025-12-31: account expiry date. -I 30: days after expiry before account locked. /etc/login.defs: PASS_MAX_DAYS for system default.

questions.question: What is the purpose of /proc filesystem?
options: A virtual filesystem presenting kernel and process information as files — /proc/cpuinfo (CPU info), /proc/meminfo (memory), /proc/PID/ (per-process info), /proc/sys/ (kernel parameters tunable via sysctl). Not on disk — exists only in memory
questions.explanation: /proc: read kernel state. /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward: IP forwarding. sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1: change via sysctl. /etc/sysctl.conf: persistent changes. /proc/PID/: process memory maps, open files, status. cat /proc/cpuinfo: CPU details. /proc/mounts: current mounts.

questions.question: How do you create a cron job that runs a script every weekday at 8am?
questions.explanation: Cron format: MIN HOUR DOM MON DOW COMMAND. 0 8 * * 1-5 = minute 0, hour 8, any day, any month, Mon-Fri (1-5). crontab -e: edit user crontab. Redirect output: 0 8 * * 1-5 /script >> /var/log/script.log 2>&1. Run as root: use /etc/crontab with user field.

questions.question: What command displays all listening TCP/UDP ports and the processes using them?
questions.explanation: ss -tulnp: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -n numeric (no name resolution), -p show process. Shows: port, state, PID, process name. Requires root for all PIDs. netstat -tulnp: older equivalent (net-tools package). lsof -i :80: what's using port 80. firewall-cmd --list-ports: what's open in firewall.

questions.question: How do you make a kernel parameter change persistent across reboots?
questions.explanation: Temporary: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (or echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward). Persistent: add 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1' to /etc/sysctl.conf or create /etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf. Apply without reboot: sysctl -p (reads /etc/sysctl.conf) or sysctl --system (reads all sysctl.d files).

questions.question: What is the diff between ps aux and ps -ef?
options: Both show all processes: ps aux (BSD syntax — %CPU, %MEM, VSZ, RSS columns). ps -ef (UNIX syntax — UID, PID, PPID, C, STIME, CMD columns). ps aux | grep process: find specific process. ps -ef --forest: show process tree (use pstree for better tree view)
ps aux is for BSD only
questions.explanation: ps aux: a=all users, u=user format, x=no terminal. Shows CPU%, MEM%, virtual/resident size. ps -ef: e=all processes, f=full format. Shows PPID (parent PID). Both useful: aux for resource usage, -ef for parent-child relationships. ps auxf: combined with process tree.

questions.question: How do you add a persistent environment variable for all users?
questions.explanation: /etc/environment: simple KEY=VALUE format (no bash syntax), loaded for all users. /etc/profile.d/*.sh: shell scripts sourced for all login shells (can use export, functions). ~/.bashrc: user-specific, non-login shells. ~/.bash_profile: user-specific, login shells. systemd services: set in service unit [Service] Environment=.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'nice' command?
options: Adjusts process scheduling priority (niceness) — nice -n 10 command: run with lower priority (+10 niceness). Lower niceness (-20 to 19, default 0) = higher CPU priority. renice -n 5 -p PID: change running process. Normal users: can only increase niceness. Root: can decrease
questions.explanation: Niceness: -20 (highest priority) to 19 (lowest). nice -n 5 ./heavy_job: run with niceness +5. nice -n -5 ./critical: higher priority (root only). renice 5 PID: change running process. Useful for: background batch jobs (high nice), critical services (low nice). Affects CPU scheduler only, not I/O.

questions.question: How do you configure NFS client to mount a share from server 'nfsserver'?
options: mount -t nfs nfsserver:/share /mnt/nfs; add to /etc/fstab for persistence
questions.explanation: Temporary: mount -t nfs nfsserver:/share /mnt/nfs. Persistent /etc/fstab: nfsserver:/share /mnt/nfs nfs defaults,_netdev 0 0. _netdev: wait for network before mounting. nfsstat: show NFS stats. showmount -e nfsserver: list server exports. Install nfs-utils first: dnf install nfs-utils.

questions.question: What command kills a process by name?
questions.explanation: killall httpd: send SIGTERM to all processes named httpd. pkill -f 'python script.py': match by full command line. kill PID: by process ID. kill -9 PID: SIGKILL (force, cannot be caught). kill -l: list signals. pkill -u username: kill all processes by user. SIGTERM (15): graceful. SIGKILL (9): force.

questions.question: How do you check and repair a filesystem before mounting?
questions.explanation: CRITICAL: fsck only on unmounted filesystems. -y: auto-answer yes to all repair prompts. For root filesystem: run from rescue mode or use e2fsck (ext4). xfs_repair /dev/sdb1: for XFS. fsck on mounted FS will corrupt data. Boot to rescue: systemctl rescue. e2fsck -p: auto-fix safe issues.

questions.question: What is the purpose of /etc/passwd vs /etc/shadow?
options: /etc/passwd: user account info (username, UID, GID, home, shell) — world-readable. /etc/shadow: hashed passwords + aging info — root-readable only. Password in /etc/passwd is replaced by 'x' since shadow was introduced. getent passwd: query NSS databases
questions.explanation: /etc/passwd format: username:x:UID:GID:comment:home:shell. /etc/shadow: username:HASH:lastchange:min:max:warn:inactive:expire. HASH format: $6$ = SHA-512. chage: modify shadow aging. pwck: check passwd consistency. unshadow: combine for cracking (John the Ripper).

questions.question: How do you configure SSH key-based authentication?
questions.explanation: Steps: (1) ssh-keygen -t ed25519 (modern) or -t rsa -b 4096. (2) ssh-copy-id user@server: copies ~/.ssh/id_*.pub to server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. (3) Test: ssh user@server (no password). Server: /etc/ssh/sshd_config PubkeyAuthentication yes (default). ~/.ssh permissions: 700 (dir), 600 (private key), 644 (pub key).

questions.question: What does the 'stat' command show?
options: Detailed file/filesystem statistics: inode number, size, blocks, file type, permissions (numeric and symbolic), hard link count, owner UID/GID, access/modify/change timestamps
questions.explanation: stat file: inode, size, device, permission (0644), links, UID, GID, atime (last access), mtime (last modification), ctime (last metadata change). stat -f /mnt: filesystem statistics. Use for: audit trails, inode investigation, checking when file was modified vs accessed.

questions.question: How do you configure a local DNF/YUM repository?
options: Create /etc/yum.repos.d/local.repo with baseurl=file:///path/to/repo; dnf clean all
questions.explanation: Create repo file: [local-repo] name=Local Repository baseurl=file:///mnt/iso/Packages enabled=1 gpgcheck=0. dnf clean all && dnf repolist. createrepo_c /path: create repo metadata from RPMs. Mount ISO: mount -o loop rhel.iso /mnt/iso. Useful for: air-gapped systems, offline patching.

questions.question: What is firewalld zone and which zone is default?
options: Firewalld uses zones to define trust levels for network connections — default is 'public'. Zones: trusted (all traffic), public (default for most), home, work, dmz, drop (all incoming dropped). Assign interfaces to zones. Zone-specific rules
Zones only apply to physical interfaces
questions.explanation: Zones: trusted→public→home→work→dmz→drop (descending trust). firewall-cmd --get-default-zone. firewall-cmd --set-default-zone=trusted. firewall-cmd --zone=dmz --add-service=http. firewall-cmd --get-active-zones: zones + assigned interfaces. Per-zone rules apply to assigned interface's traffic.

questions.question: How do you boot into rescue mode to reset root password?
options: Interrupt GRUB → append 'rd.break' to kernel line → chroot /sysroot → passwd root
questions.explanation: Reset root password: (1) GRUB screen → 'e' to edit. (2) Find linux line → append 'rd.break' (interrupts before root mount). (3) mount -o remount,rw /sysroot. (4) chroot /sysroot. (5) passwd root. (6) touch /.autorelabel (SELinux relabel). (7) exit twice → reboot. SELinux relabel required or login fails.

questions.question: What is the difference between /etc/rc.local and systemd services?
options: rc.local: legacy SysV init script that runs commands at end of boot — still works but deprecated. systemd services: proper unit files with dependency management, parallel start, failure recovery, journald logging. Prefer systemd services for new work
questions.explanation: rc.local: /etc/rc.d/rc.local must be executable (chmod +x). Runs after all services. No error handling, no parallelism. Systemd service: create /etc/systemd/system/myscript.service [Service] ExecStart=/path/script [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target. Enable: systemctl enable myscript. Better for production.

questions.question: How do you configure virtual hosted websites in Apache (httpd)?
options: Only one website per Apache instance
Use nginx instead for virtual hosting
questions.explanation: VirtualHost: <VirtualHost *:80> ServerName www.example.com DocumentRoot /var/www/example ErrorLog /var/log/httpd/example-error.log </VirtualHost>. Each site: separate .conf in /etc/httpd/conf.d/. httpd -t: syntax check. systemctl reload httpd: apply. SELinux: chcon -Rt httpd_sys_content_t /var/www/example or use restorecon.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'journalctl --vacuum-size=500M'?
options: Reduces systemd journal storage to maximum 500MB by removing oldest entries — journals can grow large on busy systems. --vacuum-time=2weeks: remove entries older than 2 weeks. journalctl --disk-usage: check current size. /etc/systemd/journald.conf: SystemMaxUse to set persistent limit
questions.explanation: Journal management: journalctl --vacuum-size=500M (immediate cleanup). Persistent size limit: /etc/systemd/journald.conf → SystemMaxUse=500M → systemctl restart systemd-journald. journalctl --rotate: rotate log files. RuntimeMaxUse: volatile storage limit. Logs stored in /var/log/journal/ (persistent) or /run/log/journal/ (volatile).
